title: Second reader still keeps companies and associates that the sentence never ties to the person (link word belongs to another clause or object)
scenario: verifyGaps on a confirmed record. 'Trevor Milton, the CEO of Nikola, criticised Ford.' keeps Ford with role 'chief executive'. 'Trevor Milton founded Nikola and Ford launched a truck.' keeps Ford as 'founder'. 'Trevor Milton and Ford CEO Jim Farley met.' and 'Trevor Milton, CEO of Nikola, criticised Jim Farley' keep Farley as a trusted associate. That associate then reaches relatedParties (report.js:1056), the watchlist screens and the network reference list.
fix: In linkBetween, make the link word govern the target. Between the link word nearest the target and the target, allow only function words (at, of, in, for, with, on, the, a, its, board of, called). Reject the stretch when another capitalised organisation run or a second verb appears in it. Count TIE_WORDS for people only in the same way, never a title word inside the other person's own run ('Ford CEO Jim Farley'). Add these four sentences as regression tests.
evidence: Temporary jest test fed 23 sentences through verifyGaps with startState Trevor Milton/Nikola. The cases above returned threads; the Ford/Farley cross-sentence cases are dropped correctly.
verifyNote: I reproduced all four cases through the real verifyGaps call. Ford came back as a company (roles 'chief executive' and 'founder'), and Jim Farley came back twice as an associate. linkBetween only looks for a link word anywhere in the stretch. A trusted associate reaches relatedParties (report.js:1054), the watchlist screens and the network matching.
betterFix: Make the link word the one that governs the target. For companies, require the nearest link word to sit next to the target, with only function words between them. Reject the stretch if it holds a second finite verb or another organisation's capitalised run. For people, ignore title words inside the other person's own capitalised run ('Ford CEO Jim Farley'). Add all four sentences as regression tests.

title: A company confirmed from the user's network is classed 'other' in the network pairing: the seed branch is dead, juniors are suggested as references, and investors are never looked up
scenario: The user confirms 'John Smith at Acme Robotics'. deepCheck seeds the thread with why 'the company assumed from your network', and report.company is null. companiesOf's GIVEN regex misses it, so the tie is 'other'. Result: self gets basis 'tied-company' and says 'That is not their current company'. A Summer Intern and an Associate at Acme become the top two reference calls, which bypasses the rule of senior staff only and at most one at the current company. investorCompanies (deep.js:77) skips Acme.
fix: Add 'the company assumed from your network' (import ASSUMED_COMPANY) to GIVEN so the company is tie 'current'. Fall back to report.assumedCompany / state.networkSeed.company in companiesOf, investorsOf and deep.js investorCompanies. Add a test where seededCompany is set and report.company is null, expecting basis 'seed' and no junior references.
evidence: buildNetworkLinks with report {company:null, threads:[{kind:'company',value:'Acme Robotics',why:'the company assumed from your network'}]}, seededCompany 'Acme Robotics': companiesOf tie 'other'; self.basis 'tied-company'; references = Amy Intern, Bob Junior.
verifyNote: I reproduced it. companiesOf returns tie 'other' for the ASSUMED_COMPANY thread because GIVEN only matches 'the company given' and 'most sources name'. self.basis comes out as 'tied-company' with the wrong note 'not their current company'. The references are Amy Intern and Bob Junior, which skips the senior-only rule for the current company.
betterFix: Export ASSUMED_COMPANY from deepCheck and add it to GIVEN, so the thread is tie 'current' and the seed branch (basis 'seed') can fire. Also fall back to report.assumedCompany in companiesOf and investorsOf when report.company is null. Add a test: seeded company, null company, juniors excluded, basis 'seed'.

title: A set but malformed FOUNDER_ALLOWED_EMAILS parses to empty and silently opens the site to every Google account
scenario: The owner sets FOUNDER_ALLOWED_EMAILS to '"owner@gmail.com"' (quotes pasted into the Vercel UI), 'owner@gmail' or 'owner'. parseAllowList returns no emails and no domains, so allowListActive is false. Every Google account can then sign in and run deep checks, though the owner believes the site is restricted. The comment 'ignored rather than widening the list' does not hold when every entry is ignored.
fix: Strip surrounding quotes and a 'mailto:' prefix from each item. When the raw value is non-blank but nothing valid parses, fail closed: refuse everyone except the dev user and log a clear error at startup. Expose parse warnings in env-check (development only).
evidence: parseAllowList('"owner@gmail.com"') -> {emails:[],domains:[]}, allowListActive false, emailAllowed(any) true. 'mailto:owner@gmail.com' parses as an email that never matches.
verifyNote: I reproduced it. A quoted value, single quotes, or 'owner@gmail' all parse to an empty list. allowListActive is then false and emailAllowed(stranger) returns true, so every Google account can sign in. 'mailto:owner@gmail.com' parses as an address that never matches, which locks everyone out instead.
betterFix: Strip quote characters and any 'mailto:' prefix from each item. If the raw value is not blank but nothing valid parses, fail closed: the list counts as active and is empty, so only the local dev user gets in. Log one clear startup error.

title: In production with no allow-list, any Google account can run model debug runs, with no cap across accounts
scenario: FOUNDER_ALLOWED_EMAILS is unset (the default). A stranger signs in with several throwaway Google accounts and loops /api/debug/llm-check?run=brief. Each account gets 10 runs an hour. The shared ':run:all' cap applies only on previews, so production has no limit across accounts, and the free model allowances run out.
fix: In production, return 404 unless allowListActive() and the account is on the list (the owner always sets the list to use debug routes). Also apply the shared hourly cap (the ':run:all' slot) in production, not only on previews.
evidence: Read debugAccess: production branch only requires getUserId; `shared` slot is gated on `preview && costly`.
verifyNote: The code matches the description: in production there is no shared cap across accounts. But FOUNDER-CHECK.md documents an unset list as 'any Google account', and the same accounts can already run costly deep checks. So this is a design choice, and the debug routes add little exposure beyond it.
betterFix: If tightened, make production debug routes return 404 unless allowListActive() is true and the account is on the list, and apply the ':run:all' shared cap in production too. Low priority.

title: Company lookup's 'incomplete' flag is computed but never read, so the alphabetical LIMIT cut stays silent
scenario: A large network, with targets like 'google' (LIKE 'google %') or multi-word keys (LIKE '%k%'). The SQL candidate rows pass LIMIT cap*targets*2 before companyMatch/companyFormMatch filters them. The outer ORDER BY lower(name) cuts late-alphabet true matches. findContactsAtCompaniesCareful returns incomplete:true, but networkForReport reads only rows and truncated, so no note appears.
fix: In networkForReport, read got.companies.incomplete and got.investors.incomplete and add a note ('Not every contact at their companies could be read'). Better, order the outer query by company_key, rn rather than by name, so a cut drops the lowest-ranked rows per company.
evidence: store.js returns { rows, truncated, incomplete }; networkLink asRows/asTruncated never touch `incomplete` (grep).
verifyNote: store.js:416 returns incomplete, but networkForReport reads only rows and truncated, so nothing ever reads it. The cut is real: the outer ORDER BY lower(name) LIMIT drops matches late in the alphabet when many company keys come through the similar LIKE. It only happens with large networks and big-company targets.
betterFix: In networkForReport, when got.companies.incomplete or got.investors.incomplete is set, add a note saying not every contact at those companies could be read. Order the outer query by rn, company_key instead of by name, so a cut drops the lowest-ranked rows first.
